title: Submit a claim

claims.claim: Walk through the New Claim form to create and submit a CMS-1500-based claim to the payer via the Stedi clearinghouse (837P JSON).

checks.pattern: {isEditMode ? '✏️ Edit Billing Claim' : 'CMS-1500 Health Insurance Claim Form'}

claims.claim: Before you start: the patient visit has been completed and signed by the rendering provider.

checks.pattern: 'No patients with billing-ready visits. A visit must have a completed, signed progress note to be eligible for claim submission.'

claims.claim: Before you start: diagnosis (ICD-10) and procedure (CPT/HCPCS) codes are confirmed.

checks.pattern: description: 'Add at least 1 ICD-10 and 1 CPT/HCPCS code before submitting.',

claims.claim: Before you start: you have the biller role, or admin.
claims.finding: Billing-lead, coder, third-party biller, clinician and other medical roles can submit too (auth-helpers.ts:332-338).

claims.claim: §1 Insurance Type — Insurance type selector (Medicare · Medicaid · Tricare · Champva · Group Health Plan · FECA Blk Lung · Other). (Steps: Complete §1 — Insurance Type. Select the appropriate insurance type from the dropdown. This drives payer-specific validation rules downstream. Caption: §1 Insurance Type and §2 Patient Name are the first fields.)
claims.finding: The claim form has no insurance-type selector. Its first claim fields are Payer Name, Payer ID and Insured's ID Number (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:151-201), after the patient picker.
claims.proposed_text: §1 / §1a — Payer Name, Payer ID and Insured's ID Number. There is no insurance-type selector.

claims.claim: §2 Patient Name — patient_last_name, patient_first_name, patient_middle_initial, patient_suffix.
claims.finding: Box 2 is one field, "Patient's Name (Last, First, Middle)" (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:250); there are no separate last/first/middle/suffix fields.
claims.proposed_text: §2 Patient's Name — one field, Last, First, Middle.

claims.claim: §4 Insured Name — insured_last_name, insured_first_name, insured_middle_initial.
claims.finding: Box 4 is one field, "Insured's Name (Last, First, Middle)" (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:458).
claims.proposed_text: §4 Insured's Name — one field, Last, First, Middle.

claims.claim: §5 Patient Address — patient_address, patient_city, patient_state, patient_zip, patient_phone.
claims.finding: Box 5 has Patient's Address (Street), City, State and Zip Code, but no phone field (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:348-417).
claims.proposed_text: §5 Patient's Address — street, city, state, ZIP code.

claims.claim: §6 Patient Relationship to Insured — Relationship selector (Self · Spouse · Child · Other). If the patient is the subscriber, select Self. For dependents, select Spouse, Child, or Other.
§7 Insured Address — insured_address, insured_city, insured_state, insured_zip, insured_phone.
claims.finding: Box 7 has Insured's Address (Street), City, State and Zip Code, but no phone field (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:472-531).
claims.proposed_text: §7 Insured's Address — street, city, state, ZIP code.

claims.claim: §8 Reserved — Reserved field (read-only; populated per payer requirements).
claims.finding: There is no reserved Box 8 field. In that part of the form the biller edits Employment Status and Marital Status (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:591-640), which are auto-filled from the patient record.
claims.proposed_text: Patient status — Employment Status and Marital Status selectors, filled from the patient record.

claims.claim: §10 Condition Related To — Checkboxes: Employment (current or previous) · Auto Accident (with state) · Other Accident. Leave all boxes unchecked for standard illness/injury.
§17 Referring Provider — referring_provider_name, referring_provider_npi — auto-filled from the patient's referring physician on record. Correct them if the referral is different for this claim.

§21 Diagnosis Codes — ICD-10 codes A through L (up to 12). Add up to 12 ICD-10 codes using the code search. The first code entered becomes pointer A and is required. Additional codes (B–L) are optional. Diagnosis codes A–L are entered in the §21 grid.
§24A Date of Service — date_of_service_from, date_of_service_to. (Step: Enter the date of service range.)
claims.finding: Each service line has one Date of Service (formData.dateOfService, BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1150-1162; line.dateOfService for added lines); there is no from/to range.
claims.proposed_text: §24A Date of Service — one date per service line.

claims.claim: §24B Place of Service (POS) — POS code selector (e.g., 11 Office · 12 Home · 31 SNF). The POS code is auto-derived from the visit's service location; override it if needed.

checks.note: a missing POS is refused at submit

claims.finding: The POS comes from the place of service the provider confirmed in the visit (Section 2), else the appointment's POS; there is no default (posDerivation.ts:13-28). A claim with no POS is refused at submit (PR #3854).

claims.claim: §24D Procedure Code + Modifiers — cpt_hcpcs_code, modifier_1, modifier_2, modifier_3, modifier_4. (Step: Enter the CPT/HCPCS code and up to four modifiers.)
claims.finding: Each service line has one Procedures/CPT Code and one Modifier box of two characters (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1245-1263; ServiceLine.modifier at :41).
claims.proposed_text: §24D — Procedure (CPT/HCPCS) code and one modifier per line.

claims.claim: §24E Diagnosis Pointer — Pointer(s) linking procedure to §21 diagnosis codes (A–L). (Step: Select the diagnosis pointer(s) from the codes entered in §21.)
claims.finding: The pointer is typed as letters (e.g. A,B,C) in a text box, not picked from a list.

claims.claim: §24F Charges — charge_amount per line. §24G Units — units per line.
§24H EPSDT / Family Plan — EPSDT indicator checkbox. (Step: Check EPSDT if applicable.)
claims.finding: 24H is a text box (placeholder "E"), hidden until "Show Additional Charge Fields (24H–24J)" is clicked. On line 1 it is not connected to any field, so what you type is not saved (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1505-1513); on added lines it is (:1452-1458).
claims.proposed_text: §24H EPSDT / Family Plan — a text box under Show Additional Charge Fields (24H–24J). Only added lines (2 onward) keep a value.

claims.claim: §24I ID Qualifier / §24J Rendering Provider NPI — Qualifier code for the rendering provider ID type; rendering_provider_npi. (Step: §24I / §24J: Confirm the ID qualifier and rendering provider NPI (auto-populated from the visit record).)

checks.note: true only if line 1's 24I/24J boxes hold a value

claims.finding: Line 1's 24I "ID Qualifier" and 24J "Rendering Provider NPI (line-level)" boxes have no value or onChange: they are empty and anything typed is dropped (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1515-1533). Added lines have a 24J Rendering NPI box that is saved, and no 24I box (:1461-1468). The rendering provider NPI that is auto-filled is the one in Box 31 "Rendering Provider NPI".
claims.proposed_text: The rendering provider's NPI is filled in Box 31 (Rendering Provider NPI). Added service lines can override it in 24J Rendering NPI.

claims.claim: §25 Federal Tax ID — federal_tax_id (EIN or SSN toggle). Verify the EIN is correct for the billing entity.
§26 Patient Account Number — patient_account_number (auto-populated from the patient record).
§27 Accept Assignment — Accept Assignment toggle (Yes / No). Confirm the toggle matches your payer contract.
§28 Total Charge — Calculated automatically from §24F line totals.

checks.pattern: Adds up every line in Section 24

claims.claim: §29 Amount Paid — amount_paid (patient or other payer payment received prior to submission).
claims.finding: The claim form has no Box 29 Amount Paid field. Section 25-30 has Tax ID Number, Patient Account #, Accept Assignment, Total Charge and Balance Due (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1551-1680).
claims.proposed_text: There is no §29 Amount Paid field on the claim form.

claims.claim: §30 Balance Due — Calculated automatically (§28 minus §29). §28 Total Charge and §30 Balance Due are read-only calculated fields.

checks.note: true only if Balance Due is not hand-editable

claims.finding: Total Charge is read-only and calculated, but Balance Due is an ordinary editable box (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1660-1678) that starts at 0.00 and is not calculated from anything (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:513).
claims.proposed_text: §28 Total Charge is read-only and adds up every Section 24 line. §30 Balance Due is entered by hand.

proposed_checks.pattern: Adds up every line in Section 24

claims.claim: §31 Provider Signature — Digital provider signature captured during visit attestation.
claims.finding: The form's Box 31 is "31. Rendering Provider" with Provider Name, Taxonomy and Rendering Provider NPI (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1705-1745). The claim form shows no signature.
claims.proposed_text: §31 Rendering Provider — provider name, taxonomy and NPI.

claims.claim: §32 Service Facility — service_facility_name, service_facility_address, service_facility_npi. Confirm addresses and NPIs match your payer enrollment.
claims.finding: The facility name and 32a NPI show only when the place of service names a facility (ServiceFacilityBox32.tsx:17-18).

claims.claim: §33 Billing Provider — billing_provider_name, billing_provider_address, billing_provider_npi, billing_provider_phone.
Open the claim form. Navigate to /facility/{facility_uuid}/billing/new — the New Claim form opens as a full page. (Billers also reach it by clicking Edit on a claim in the Work Queue.)
Complete §2 — Patient Name. Search for the patient by last name or date of birth.

checks.note: true only if the picker's search text includes the date of birth

claims.finding: The patient picker searches name or MRN ("Search patient name or MRN...", search value = full name + MRN, BillingSubmitPatientSelector.tsx:534-544), not date of birth. It lists only patients with a billing-ready visit (a completed, signed progress note, :538).
claims.proposed_text: Select the patient. The picker searches by name or MRN and lists only patients with a visit that has a completed, signed progress note.

claims.claim: Selecting an existing patient auto-fills §4 Insured Name, §5 Patient Address, §17 Referring Provider, §26 Patient Account Number, and §29 Amount Paid from the patient record.
claims.finding: §4, §5, §17 and §26 are filled from the patient (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:1622-1651). There is no §29 Amount Paid field to fill. The same step also fills date of birth, sex, marital and employment status, §7 insured address, §10 conditions and §27 accept assignment.
claims.proposed_text: Selecting a patient fills §2 name, date of birth and sex, §4 Insured Name, §5 Patient Address, §7 Insured Address, §10 Condition Related To, §17 Referring Provider, §26 Patient Account Number and §27 Accept Assignment from the patient record.

claims.claim: Verify §4 through §8. Confirm the insured name and address match the insurance card. Correct any discrepancies before proceeding — payer rejections for demographic mismatches are common.
claims.finding: Workflow advice and a payer-behavior statement; not checkable from code.

claims.claim: Add service lines — §24A through §24J. Click + Add Line for each procedure.
claims.finding: The button that adds a service line is labelled "Add Charge" (BillingSubmitFormFields.tsx:1484-1485). Line 1 is filled from the first CPT code in Billing codes & procedures.
claims.proposed_text: Add service lines — §24A through §24J. Click + Add Charge for each additional procedure.

claims.claim: Service lines can be dragged to reorder; the CMS-1500 Box 24 line numbering re-asserts automatically after a move.

checks.note: true only if the Section 24 service lines themselves are draggable

claims.finding: The service lines in Section 24 cannot be dragged. What drags is the CPT row list in "Billing codes & procedures" (BillingCodeEntry.tsx, dnd-kit); a drop there re-fills Box 24 line 1 from the first CPT by position (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:2291-2304, computeBox24OnReorder).
claims.proposed_text: CPT codes in Billing codes & procedures can be dragged to reorder; after a move, Box 24 is filled again from the new order.

claims.claim: Complete §25 through §33. These fields are generally auto-populated from your facility and provider configuration.
Click Save Draft to save without submitting, or Submit Claim to send it to the payer through Stedi. (A confirmation prompt appears before either action completes.)

checks.note: the save button label as the page writes it

checks.pattern: setSavingModalMessage(isEditMode ? 'Save changes to this claim?' : 'Save this claim as draft?');
setSavingModalMessage(isEditMode ? 'Update and submit this claim?' : 'Create and submit this claim?');

claims.finding: The save button reads "Save Changes" ("No Changes" and disabled when nothing has changed), not "Save Draft" (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:5423-5435). Submit Claim and both confirmation prompts are as described.
claims.proposed_text: Click Save Changes to save without submitting, or Submit Claim to send it to the payer through Stedi. A confirmation prompt appears before either action completes.

proposed_checks.pattern: setSavingModalMessage(isEditMode ? 'Save changes to this claim?' : 'Save this claim as draft?');
setSavingModalMessage(isEditMode ? 'Update and submit this claim?' : 'Create and submit this claim?');

claims.claim: The rendering provider NPI in §24J must match the NPI on file with the payer. Submitting with a group NPI in §24J instead of the individual NPI is a common rejection cause for Medicare claims.

checks.pattern: //   provider with an active, Medicare-enrolled, 10-digit Type-1 NPI.

claims.finding: Payer rule; the check confirms the product resolves the rendering provider to an individual (Type-1) NPI.

claims.claim: A Save Draft keeps the claim as a draft; Submit Claim sends it to Stedi and advances it toward Submitted.

checks.note: true only if saving always leaves the claim a draft

claims.finding: Saving a new claim stores it as Draft, but saving an existing claim keeps its current status (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:3822-3827). After a successful Stedi send the claim is Submitted; a Stedi rejection makes it Rejected (NewBillingSubmitPage.tsx:4965).
claims.proposed_text: Saving a new claim stores it as a draft; saving an existing claim keeps its status. Submit Claim sends it to Stedi; it becomes Submitted when Stedi accepts it, or Rejected when Stedi rejects it.

claims.claim: The claim appears in the Work Queue tied to its encounter, where you can track and set its Claim Status.
claims.finding: It appears only when an appointment matches it (by visit or by patient and date of service); a claim with no matching appointment in the date range does not show.

claims.claim: Claims are generated automatically from a completed visit and appear in the Work Queue — you do not need to create them manually.
Use the claim form for claims that need to be entered or corrected outside the normal visit workflow (e.g., corrected claims, late charges), reached via Edit in the Work Queue or /billing/new.
Submit Claim disabled or errors — One or more required fields missing or invalid — Scroll through the form — required fields are outlined in red.
Payer rejects claim for NPI mismatch — Group NPI used in §24J instead of individual NPI — Update the rendering provider's NPI in HR & Compliance, then resubmit.
§28 Total Charge calculates as zero — No service lines added, or charge amounts left blank — Add at least one §24 line with a non-zero charge.

checks.pattern: {/* Box 28 = total of every Section 24 line (CMS 100-04 Ch. 26 Item 28) */}

claims.claim: Claim stuck at Exported — Stedi credentials missing, webhook not wired, or payer not enrolled — Have your administrator verify the Stedi setup in Billing Setup and confirm payer enrollment is Active.

checks.note: true only if an Exported claim is waiting on a Stedi send

claims.finding: Exported only means the claim was exported as a PDF or JSON file (BillingDashboard.tsx:1253-1256); no code sends Exported claims to Stedi, so credentials, webhooks and enrollment cannot keep a claim there. There is no "Billing Setup" screen; enrollment is on Payer Enrollment (Quick Actions), whose good state is ACTIVE (StediEnrollmentPage.tsx:292).
claims.proposed_text: Claim stays at Exported — exporting a PDF or JSON does not send the claim. Open it and click Submit Claim. If Stedi refuses it for enrollment, check Payer Enrollment (Quick Actions) and confirm the provider's enrollment is ACTIVE.

proposed_checks.pattern: "Claim has been exported as PDF or JSON. Ready to submit.",
